title: How are you getting you game beta tested?
author: Dukisef
selftext:
I for one am terrified of leaving my game out there due to the fear of it being cloned. So i've turned to my friends and family but they are not really gamers.

Any advice or a service with NDA that I can maybe pay to get it tested?

Or do I wait to see if I manage to get a publisher so they can deal with QA?

comments.author: PupperRobot
comments.body:
My game is the "spiritual successor" of a game from the 90s and I joined a few communities that still play that game. I asked them to play test it on steam. I also added a robust analytics system so I can see how the game is played without asking for direct feedback. 

Also my friends help out with testing

comments.author: boxing-boxing
comments.body:
Just don’t tell anyone it’s beta,  put it out there people will show up.

Thats how I started, just hit my 700th account sign up today (sign up not required to play)

replies.author: SoftwareDifficult186
replies.body: I would make a wild guess and say it’s about boxing

comments.author: WhosLive
comments.body: If you're worried about cloning, a few things usually help: keep a playable slice rather than the full game, ship a build with no source and no unreleased content, and put it behind a Steam playtest or a private itch.io page with a password. Cloning of a game that isn't finished is rarer than people fear, since most of the value is in the polish and the content you haven't shown yet. For testers who actually play games, it's worth trying small Discord servers for your genre and offering a few keys in exchange for a short written feedback form. Asking for a specific thing (first 10 minutes, where they got confused, where they quit) gets far better feedback than 'what do you think'. Short NDAs from a tester are fine to ask for, but paid QA services are usually overkill before you have a build that's stable.

comments.author: Ravenravine2
comments.body: Easy, just get better friends. (Gamer friends) ;)

replies.author: MessageSelfdestructs
replies.body: It's quite limiting to only let your game be tested by gamers imho.

comments.author: SniperArms
comments.body: honestly a basic browser game idea is rarely worth a paid NDA service at this stage, cloning risk is much smaller than getting zero feedback. i'd find a few small communities of people who actually play your genre and ask for 10 minutes of play with one specific question, then watch where they get stuck. even 5 strangers will show you more than friends and family will.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
Just get over yourself and stop pretending you have the next big thing...

I had an open beta on Steam for my own two games, and that gave me great feedback.

replies.author: bunnyUFO
replies.body:
Yeah copycats copy success not ideas.

If game is unknown no I'm one will you.

 If you already have a success indicator like wish lists, community, interests in videos,going viral on media, or being the top game at steam fest, you'll be fine even if someone copies you.
